races.name: Excell Supply Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ancient Realm
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and entirely unexposed for Julie Camacho, whose 3/16 14-day strike rate warrants respect; running style completely unknown, making scenario assessment impossible, but the trainer angle keeps her in play on debut.

runners_data.name: Dream Vega
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 7f on Good ground including a runner-up, so the trip and conditions are confirmed positives; naturally prominent, Ed Walker's 8/34 recent form is solid, and she is the best-credentialled placed runner in this field on form.

runners_data.name: Golden Mabel
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a pronounced habit of fading in the finish and a deeply uninspiring recent record of three eights and a seven; Good ground is familiar but the fade flag makes her a difficult proposition even in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Mint
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Daniel & Claire Kubler with no public form to assess and an unknown running style; the stable's modest 1/7 14-day record offers little encouragement, and she is essentially a wildcard.

runners_data.name: Moonlight Melody
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's hold-up filly has placed fourth and fifth in her two starts — both at shorter trips — so stepping up to 7f could unlock more; Good going is fine, and a patient Donald McCain-McCain McCain McCain McCain ride from Allan suits if the pace is genuine.

runners_data.name: Secret Oath
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's 2-year-old returning after 379 days off is the pace map's key horse — she holds the confirmed front-running role but that long layoff is a major fitness concern; her Good-ground form (placed over 5-6f) is solid but she races out of her usual age group and the absence cannot be ignored.

runners_data.name: Something Coming
runners_data.note: Peter Chapple-Hyam's filly has a detailed form string showing two seconds and a third at 7f, though almost exclusively on Standard artificial surfaces (1/6 on Good); the step to Chester's Good turf is an untested variable, but her course-specific ability to finish close makes her quietly interesting.

runners_data.name: Venetian Sky
runners_data.note: William Haggas's hold-up filly has placed fourth-fourth-third across 7f on Good ground — her optimal conditions — and Haggas's 7/29 14-day record shows the yard is in form; Harry Davies takes the ride on a filly whose profile is tailor-made for a steadily-run race she can close into.

runners_data.name: Veronique
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding debut runner with zero form to dissect but a trainer firing at 13/61 over 14 days, which is the strongest stable form in this field; completely unknown in terms of style, she carries the biggest upside uncertainty of the three debutants.

races.paceDynamic: Secret Oath is the lone confirmed front-runner here, and with no other horse clearly looking to press for the lead, she is likely to dictate from the front at a comfortable, even tempo on Good ground around Chester's tight turns. Dream Vega is the only other prominent-style runner, but she is a hold-up horse displaced slightly forward and unlikely to apply serious early pressure. With the pace likely to be honest but uncontested and sustainable rather than truly searching, the field risks being drawn into a steadily-run affair where position off the bend becomes critical. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a meaningful turn of foot — specifically Venetian Sky, Moonlight Melody and Golden Mabel — who can come from off the pace and exploit any faltering leader in the final furlong, though Chester's short straight means timing the run will be essential.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sole Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Oath dictates an uncontested, evenly-measured gallop and the field is strung out by Chester's bends before the short straight
scenarios.body: Secret Oath goes unchallenged to the front, sets an energy-conserving pace that suits her natural front-running tendency, and has enough in reserve to repel challengers through the tight 2f home straight; Dream Vega, pressing from the prominent position, is best placed of the chasers if she can quicken off the steady tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough to set up a sprint finish and those ridden quietly get clear runs rounding the home turn
scenarios.body: Venetian Sky and Moonlight Melody, held off the pace, find the tempo sufficient to produce a strong late run through the short straight; Chester's tight configuration is a risk but their proven ability on Good ground and over 7f gives them a credible closing profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Falters, Closers Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Oath — returning after 379 days off — hits the wall late having set a strong early tempo and the field bunches in the straight
scenarios.body: A long absence for Secret Oath means fitness questions are legitimate; if she ties up in the final furlong, hold-up horses including Venetian Sky and Something Coming, who has shown ability to finish off races at 7f, surge past a weakening leaderboard.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutants Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three lightly-raced unknown-style runners — Veronique, Ancient Realm or Mint — carries hidden ability and produces an unexposed performance
scenarios.body: Andrew Balding's Veronique from a yard in strong 14-day form (13/61) or Julie Camacho's Ancient Realm could bypass the pace question entirely if they carry class that the bare form of the field does not reflect; on debut, tactics are irrelevant and raw talent can bulldoze the shape entirely.

watchPoints.text: Secret Oath's 379-day absence is the race's central risk factor — if her fitness gives way in the final furlong after leading, the entire pace map collapses and hold-up horses will benefit disproportionately.

Venetian Sky's ability to get a clear run around Chester's tight home turn is critical — Harry Davies must commit early enough to avoid a traffic problem in the short 2f straight, as a blocked run here is race-ending.

The three debutants (Veronique, Ancient Realm, Mint) represent genuine unknown quantities; if any carry significant undemonstrated ability, they could override the pace shape entirely and make scenario analysis redundant.

Dream Vega's draw and early position will be key — if she cannot press Secret Oath naturally, she risks being caught in a mid-pack squeeze around the turns and losing the prominent berth that defines her best form.

Something Coming's near-exclusive artificial-surface form record (1/6 on Good) means Chester's turf on Good going is an untested element; her finishing style suits the shape but ground suitability is an open question.

races.name: John Smith's Handicap

runners_data.name: Secret Mistral
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up horse in strong recent form (2-2-3-8-2), very effective on Good ground (8/15 similar-going entries) and over 5f at a similar track level; Myla Coppins takes the 7lb claim which aids the weight, but this horse needs a gap to appear in Chester's short straight and getting that from a rear position in a 13-runner field is far from guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Secret Mistral has been placed in four of her last five starts, including a second last time out, though she remains without a win in that spell. She has form over today's trip and ground, carries 140lb from stall 2, and sits square in midfield on our figures.

runners_data.name: Beauzon
runners_data.note: Ian Williams seven-year-old returning after 117 days off, but his recent form shows four consecutive wins at Southwell over 6f — the step back to 5f on Good turf at Chester is a notable switch in conditions, and Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim is a minor bonus; his prominent style means he can at least get a good position, but the form has been built on a different surface.
runners_data.comment: Beauzon strung together five wins in a row before a below-par run last time out, and has had 117 days since to recover. Despite that sequence, he anchors our figures at the bottom of this field, though he does have form over today's trip and ground, carrying 137lb from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Beaumadier
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane runner who raced just 9 days ago, with two recent placings on Good ground suggesting the conditions suit; a genuine hold-up horse who has been placed twice in 15 similar-going runs, Hope Regan's 7lb claim helps, but being a true rear-ranker means finding room in this congested Chester straight will be the key challenge.
runners_data.comment: Beaumadier has been in the frame with a second and third in his last two starts, and he's fresh from a run just nine days ago. He has form over today's trip and ground, carries 136lb from stall 6, but sits only ninth on our figures.

runners_data.name: Miraculous
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby four-year-old with strong Good ground form (11/15) and a placing record that includes recent 5f and 6f efforts; David Allan has experience placing horses from the back, but this is a hold-up type who will need the pace to be honest and the field to fan out to get a clear run in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Miraculous tops our figures here, backed by one of the sharpest speed figures in the race and a creditable third three starts back. Quick to back up racing just eight days ago, he has form over today's trip and ground from stall 13, with his only blot a winless run in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: The Flying Seagull
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's four-year-old carries a hood and is a genuine hold-up performer whose natural rear-of-field role cannot be fulfilled here — the surplus of closers means he is effectively operating from midfield out of his preferred position, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) tempers expectations; his recent 5f Good ground form is modest (3rd best finish a 3rd at 6f), making this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: The Flying Seagull ran into a solid third last time out, placing him among the leading threats on our figures despite remaining winless in his last five starts. An unplaced effort two starts back is the blot, but he has form over today's trip and ground and carries 135lb from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Intervention
runners_data.note: Veteran nine-year-old from Michael Appleby's yard who has not placed in any of his five most recent runs on similar going; a true hold-up horse forced into midfield by the field dynamics, and with a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91, his chance in the dominant race shape is materially discounted — 27 days since last run and no recent form to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Intervention's finishing positions make grim reading, with nothing better than a fourth in his last six starts, yet he owns one of the fastest speed figures in this race. He has form over today's trip and ground and carries 134lb from stall 11, with turning that raw pace into a finishing effort the target.

runners_data.name: Alfa Duplicate
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's three-year-old is the key pace-setter in this race; with wins on Soft and Standard surfaces, the Good turf ground is a minor query (0W0P in 3 similar-going runs), but his front-running style at Chester — where leaders who control their own pace have a clear advantage — makes him the structural pivot of the entire race shape.
runners_data.comment: Alfa Duplicate won three of her last six starts and rates second on our figures, marking her a leading threat, though her last two runs have dipped below that level. Her trainer is out of form at 0% over the last fortnight, the obvious concern, but she does have form over today's trip and ground.

runners_data.name: General Assembly
runners_data.note: Clare Hobson five-year-old off 54 days, his longest break in recent runs, and a genuine hold-up type whose best recent form on similar going is a pair of second-place finishes on Standard; the field depth at the rear means he cannot race from his natural position, and his trainer's T14 record of 0/3 offers no encouragement.
runners_data.comment: General Assembly was unplaced last time out, though a pair of seconds earlier in that sequence shows he retains some ability, despite being without a win in his last five starts. He has form over today's trip and ground, carries 133lb from stall 4, and sits mid-pack on our figures following a 54-day absence.

runners_data.name: Maharajas Express
runners_data.note: Ian Williams second string ridden by Edward Greatrex, racing just 5 days after his last start; his prominent style makes him one of the most naturally positioned horses to track Alfa Duplicate, and he has placed five times in 15 similar-going runs, suggesting Good turf at 5f is within his compass — freshness after a 5-day turnaround is the key fitness query.
runners_data.comment: Maharajas Express was below-par last time out, continuing a decline from a third furthest back in this sequence, and remains without a win in his last five starts. Quick to return just five days on, he has form over today's trip and ground but sits only midfield on our figures.

runners_data.name: Ay Gee Ell
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey four-year-old fitted with a tv visor, with a recent ninth on Good ground at 5f and no wins on similar going (0W1P in 15 runs); a true hold-up type who is pushed into midfield by the crowd at the rear of this field, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) reflects that his natural running style cannot be expressed here.
runners_data.comment: Ay Gee Ell has been on a downward curve, following two thirds further back with progressively modest efforts and a below-par run last time out, remaining without a win in his last six starts. He has form over today's trip and ground, carries 132lb from stall 5, and still ranks around midfield on our figures.

runners_data.name: Coyy
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton three-year-old fitted with a hood, with excellent Good ground form (8/10) and a 5f win on Good earlier in the season; a hold-up type, but one whose form profile on this going is the strongest of the closers in the field, and Pat Cosgrave's experience navigating Chester's tight circuit gives this runner the best chance among the rear-of-field group of finding a meaningful run.

runners_data.name: Arlo's Girl
runners_data.note: Joseph Parr three-year-old who won over 5f on Standard ground earlier in her career but has not fired since, finishing 4th to 8th in her five most recent starts; a hold-up type who cannot get her natural position in this field, and her Good ground record (0W0P in 3 runs at 5f on similar going) gives little basis for confidence, with the redistribution compounding an already modest recent profile.
runners_data.comment: Arlo's Girl has struggled of late, without a top-four finish in her last three starts, and she sits near the bottom of this field on our figures. She did land a race some way back and has form over today's trip and ground, carrying 130lb from stall 10, but needs a big reversal of recent form.

runners_data.name: Knicks
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby five-year-old returning 12 days after last run, with three placings in 15 Good ground starts but no wins; another genuine rear-of-field runner who is pushed into midfield by the field's structural overcrowding at the back, and a STYLE_FIT score of 0.90 — the lowest in the race — signals the biggest mismatch between this horse's natural role and the race shape on offer.
runners_data.comment: Knicks has been a consistent also-ran, without a win in his last six starts but with nothing worse than a seventh among them. He has form over today's trip and ground, carries 127lb from stall 8, and is fit from a run just 12 days ago, though he rates only modestly on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Alfa Duplicate is the one confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 5f Chester handicap and, with no genuine pace rival likely to push him hard from the off, he should be able to settle into a controlled, sustainable gallop around the tight Chester circuit. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up horses — Secret Mistral, Beaumadier, Miraculous, The Flying Seagull, Intervention, General Assembly, Ay Gee Ell, Coyy, Arlo's Girl and Knicks all carry hold-up profiles — meaning the rear of the field will be extremely congested and many will be forced wider and earlier than ideal. Beauzon and Maharajas Express offer the most realistic threat to Alfa Duplicate's lead, likely tracking just off the pace in a prominent position, while the field holds substantially more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the back; The Flying Seagull, Intervention, General Assembly, Arlo's Girl and Ay Gee Ell are among those most likely to be shuffled into an unnatural midfield position rather than finding true cover at the rear. A sustainable, single-leader tempo on Good ground at Chester — where the straight is extremely short and position off the final turn is critical — strongly favours horses able to race prominently or just off the pace, as those buried in the hold-up pack will face a compressed finishing straight with little room to deliver a meaningful late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alfa Duplicate Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Alfa Duplicate leads unchallenged and sets a fair but not breakneck pace, allowing him to find a second gear in the short Chester straight.
scenarios.body: Alfa Duplicate dictates from the front with Beauzon and Maharajas Express tracking within striking range, and the hold-up pack never generates the momentum to reel in the leader through the tight bend and tiny straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Beauzon or Maharajas Express press Alfa Duplicate enough to soften him, leaving one of the close-tracking duo to pounce inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A fraction more pace from the prominent group takes the edge off Alfa Duplicate in the closing stages, and a horse who has tracked the leader throughout delivers a late thrust in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up runner secures an unusually forward position off the pace and benefits from a clear run around the bend to nail the leaders.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up types forced into unnatural midfield spots, the one runner that manages to find a clean passage and a clear sightline into the short straight could deliver a late burst on the Good ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough — perhaps through Beauzon pressing hard — to ensure the front-runners tie each other up and a deeper hold-up runner finds an improbable late gap.
scenarios.body: Only in a scenario where genuine pressure is applied early and the field strings out does a true closer get any real chance, but Chester's cramped straight makes this the least likely shape to reward a rearward runner.

watchPoints.text: Alfa Duplicate's sectionals out of the stalls — if he breaks sharply and is unopposed by 1f, he is likely to control the pace well enough to be a major player into the short Chester straight.

Beauzon's fitness after 117 days off the track is the key unknown; if he is rusty early and drops out of prominent contention, Maharajas Express becomes the sole chaser of Alfa Duplicate with significantly more influence on the race shape.

Watch the draw and early positioning of Coyy — if Pat Cosgrave can secure a midfield position on the inside rail rather than being trapped wide, this is the hold-up horse most likely to find a meaningful gap in the compressed straight.

The cluster of seven redistributed hold-up horses will create significant traffic through the bend; any runner drawn wide and forced to race three or four wide at Chester is effectively out of contention before the straight begins — check early running positions carefully.

Good ground is confirmed for this race and is consistent across the card — no horse faces a going concern, but Alfa Duplicate's 0W0P record specifically on Good turf (as opposed to his wins on Soft and Standard) is worth monitoring against his market price.

races.name: Tom Jones Live At Chester Racecourse Handicap (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Percy's Lad
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Kubler who has struggled to reproduce a good run consistently, posting four poor efforts in his last five; 12 days since last run is fine, but his best form came at 8f and this 7½f at Chester may not offer the late surge room his style requires.
runners_data.comment: Boasts the smartest figures in this field, backed by a good second last time out and fitness in hand from a run just 12 days ago. Drawn 4, and yet to get his head in front this spell, but clearly the leading contender here.

runners_data.name: Miami Matrix
runners_data.note: Patrick Morris's four-year-old carries headgear (p) and arrived here placed at 7f on good ground twice recently, suggesting conditions suit; his prominent style fits this Chester shape well, though 42 days off the track is a mild concern and his overall record (no win in 11 similar-going runs) suggests he finds ways to get beaten.
runners_data.comment: A leading threat on figures, with a runner-up effort three starts back the standout in this sequence, though it's a stretch after 42 days off and a below-par ninth last time out. Drawn 3, and yet to score this spell, but capable of bouncing back.

runners_data.name: Obelix
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a meaningful caution at Chester where the run-in is short; holds headgear (h) and has a win on good ground at 7f in the past, but his sim-going record is patchy and the finishing fade warning makes him a risky hold-up proposition in a race that is unlikely to set up for closers.
runners_data.comment: A leading contender who won two starts back, since dipping into modest placings including a below-par run last time out. Ran over today's trip before, fresh enough 21 days on and drawn 2, he clearly holds claims on the stronger of his recent efforts.

runners_data.name: Vixey
runners_data.note: Simon West's six-year-old has a genuinely strong recent profile — won at 7f on good ground, placed twice at that trip — and her prominent style suits Chester's front-biased geometry; no headgear concern and a fresh enough preparation at 17 days make her one of the best-positioned runners in terms of both profile and race shape fit.
runners_data.comment: Outclassed on these figures, with a lone win five starts back since fading into modest placings, an eighth last time out among them. Raced over today's trip before, fitness fine 17 days on, but a moderate speed figure leaves plenty to find from draw 8.

runners_data.name: Eagle Bay
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in this field, Harriet Bethell's three-year-old has won on good ground and at 8f, so the step back to 7½f is a query; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) is relevant only if Eagle Bay cannot hold the lead — if it does, the course bias is squarely in its favour, but the discount applies if rivals push it off the front early.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last three starts look strong on paper, yet he's ranked only ninth of ten on our figures. Ran over today's trip before and fit enough 14 days on, but hard to fancy from that lowly spot, drawn 5.

runners_data.name: He's A Gentleman
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's seven-year-old is a natural hold-up type moved into the midfield map because the race holds too many hold-up horses; his sim-going record is extremely thin (0W0P in 15 similar runs) and 102 days since last run adds fitness doubt — the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reflects that he is unlikely to operate from his ideal position here, and his form at Chester has not been strong.
runners_data.comment: Frequently placed without landing the prize, with three runner-up efforts in his last five starts, the latest of them last time out. A 102-day layoff is the obvious concern, though he's raced over today's trip before, and drawn 10, looks no better than a minor player in this company.

runners_data.name: Moon Beginnings
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse that has been mapped to midfield because of the overcrowded backmarker group; David Loughnane's four-year-old carries headgear (/es) and has been well beaten in most recent starts, with a solitary win in sim-going from eight attempts — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) is a meaningful drag on his prospects here.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent record, without a placing better than fourth in his last five starts, including two below-par efforts further back in that sequence. Fit enough 29 days on and with today's trip previously covered, drawn 9, he's more workmanlike than incisive on these figures.

runners_data.name: Paws For Thought
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's eight-year-old is flagged for fading in the finish and carries headgear (b); a natural hold-up type repositioned on the map, his sim-going record shows zero wins and just one placing in 15 comparable runs — both the style displacement and the finishing weakness combine to make this a difficult race to get involved in.
runners_data.comment: Yet to threaten the frame in this sequence, with nothing better than a fifth in his last five starts and two unplaced efforts among them. Quick enough back within 16 days and having raced over today's trip before, drawn 7 he needs more than a step forward to feature.

runners_data.name: Advance Twentyfive
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's three-year-old is a hold-up type stepping back from 10f, and his Chester debut at 7½f on good ground represents an unknown quantity; 42 days between runs is modest, and his form string includes a couple of poor finishes at 7f, making it hard to build a case for him unless the race falls apart completely.
runners_data.comment: Our figures place him above his recent form, which reads modestly with nothing better than fifth in his last five starts. Fresh from a 42-day break and with today's trip covered before, drawn 6, the scope in his figures makes him a leading threat despite that form.

runners_data.name: Giant
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse placed on the midfield map due to the congested rear-of-field picture; his sim-going record includes two placings but no wins in 15 attempts, and although he ran just nine days ago suggesting fitness, the STYLE_FIT tag (0.91) and Chester's front-biased track make it very hard to see him getting competitive.
runners_data.comment: Prop the field on official and our figures alike, last of ten, with modest placings including two unplaced efforts in his last six starts. A strong speed figure is the one plus, and though fit on a swift 9-day turnaround, he's hard to fancy from draw 1.

races.paceDynamic: Eagle Bay is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a 10-runner field over 7½f at Chester, is positioned to dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo from the front without meaningful pressure. The tight, turning nature of Chester amplifies the advantage of being on the pace — horses who secure early position around the bends will save ground and avoid the trouble that habitually engulfs the rear of a field here. He's A Gentleman, Moon Beginnings, Paws For Thought, and Giant are all true hold-up horses mapped to midfield because the race holds more off-the-pace types than the track can accommodate at the rear; of these, He's A Gentleman and Moon Beginnings are most likely to find any semblance of a forward position given their natural inclination, though even they will be behind the leaders. This race shape — a single front-runner, steady pace, with a pack of genuine hold-up horses unable to get their natural slot — strongly favours horses racing prominently or within the first three or four, as the Chester rail and bend sequence will make it extremely difficult for backmarkers to generate momentum late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eagle Bay Controls Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Eagle Bay leads from the break and no rival has the pace or inclination to challenge for the front, settling into a smooth, rail-hugging rhythm.
scenarios.body: Eagle Bay dictates from flag to finish on a track where front-runners are notoriously hard to peg back when they control their own fractions; the tight circuit means the gap to backmarkers grows incrementally with every bend negotiated cleanly. Prominent types who slot in directly behind — Vixey and Miami Matrix — are the primary beneficiaries if the leader does surrender the initiative late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Eagle Bay's early pace is just fractionally too brisk and the chasing pack of Vixey and Miami Matrix swoop past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Chester's run-in is short and front-runners who overcook the tempo by even a small margin are vulnerable to the horse sitting a length or two behind in the slipstream; Vixey's strong recent form at 7f on good ground and Miami Matrix's placed record on similar conditions make them credible overtakers in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Break Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the field strings out and creates a clear gap for runners emerging late, allowing a genuine closer to find daylight.
scenarios.body: Percy's Lad or Obelix would need an unusually messy, fast-then-slow tempo to produce the late gaps that rarely materialise at Chester; Obelix carries a fade-in-finish flag which further reduces the probability of him sustaining a winning run even if the shape opens up. This scenario is substantially discounted because so many of the natural hold-up horses here are redistibuted types unable to get to the back cleanly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Traffic Trouble
scenarios.trigger: If the tight Chester bends cause significant interference, bunching the midfield and leaving several runners unable to find a clean run.
scenarios.body: Chester's unique track geometry amplifies small errors in positioning, and a large midfield cluster of redistributed hold-up horses is precisely the environment where scrimmaging occurs; any runner that secures clean air early — Eagle Bay or Vixey — would benefit most from the chaos behind.

watchPoints.text: Eagle Bay's early jumping and positioning is the single most important moment in this race — if it leads cleanly and settles, the Chester front-runner bias makes it very difficult to catch; watch whether any rival forces it wide or challenges for the rail in the first two furlongs.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (He's A Gentleman, Moon Beginnings, Paws For Thought, Giant) will be fighting for the same midfield ground entering the first bend — congestion and interference here could compromise multiple runners simultaneously.
Obelix's fade-in-finish flag is a live concern at Chester where the straight is brutally short; if he travels well into the final bend, watch whether he finds his usual empty finish before the line.

Vixey's prominent style and recent 7f good-ground form means she is the runner most likely to capitalise if Eagle Bay weakens — watch her position entering the back straight as that will signal whether she is travelling well enough to challenge.

Miami Matrix's headgear (p) is worth tracking on debut in this equipment combination — if the blinkers sharpen his early pace and he moves up to challenge Eagle Bay, the race dynamic changes entirely and the hold-up horses become even less likely to get involved.

races.name: Tom Jones Live At Chester Racecourse Handicap (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Sujet
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a wide blinkered form profile but poor recent record (-72000); the 14-day turnaround for Declan Carroll is unremarkable and Chester's tight track makes a late rattle from the rear very difficult, compounding the style disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Sujet remains winless in his last five starts but a second among them shows he retains real ability, and he tops our figures here. Proven over today's trip and ground, he carries 144lb from stall 2, leaving the finishing effort as the main question.

runners_data.name: Lexington Jet
runners_data.note: A hold-up type whose two wins came on Standard (AW) ground, and his Good-turf record is a thin 2-from-15 with only one win; Harry Davies takes over but the trip and course cut no ice with this profile.
runners_data.comment: Lexington Jet has won twice in his last six starts but was well held last time out. Proven over today's trip and ground, he carries 141lb from stall 1 and sits only midfield on our figures, with the profile more workmanlike than progressive.

runners_data.name: Knights Gold
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer whose recent form shows consistent placed efforts at 8f on Good; Jack Doughty partners for the Newland/Insole yard who are 2-from-19 in the 14-day window, and dropping to 7½f from 8f is not a concern given his tactical speed.
runners_data.comment: Knights Gold has followed a below-par run with back-to-back thirds, and though yet to win in his last six starts, he ranks highly on our figures. Proven over today's trip and ground, he carries 137lb from stall 3, with sharpening finishing speed the one query.

runners_data.name: Indian Spirit
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won off a lower mark over a mile on Standard surfaces; the 47-day absence is a flag, Good-turf form reads 0-from-4 for wins, and getting a clear run around Chester from off the pace looks a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Indian Spirit has been unplaced in his last two starts and sits near the bottom of this field on our figures. He did land a race three starts back and has form over today's trip and ground, though a 47-day absence and stall 8 add to the task.

runners_data.name: Mission Command
runners_data.note: In-form yard (Candlish 4/21 T14) and the tongue-tie is retained, but his natural inclination to race towards the rear puts him in a compromised position here — the field's density at the back means he is likely to race further forward than ideal without getting a true hold-up role.
runners_data.comment: Mission Command was below par last time out. He won two starts back, and a pair of thirds earlier in the sequence hint at more than his rating suggests. Proven over today's trip and ground, he carries 133lb from stall 9 and needs to rediscover that form.

runners_data.name: Start Me Up
runners_data.note: The sole front runner in this field and the tactical linchpin of the race; Richard Spencer's colt has back-to-back wins at 7f and 6f on Good/Soft, and Jack Callan's 3lb claim sweetens the weight equation — he is the architect of whatever shape this race takes.
runners_data.comment: Start Me Up arrives in form, having won his last two starts after modest efforts further back, and that progressive profile makes him our pick. Proven over today's trip and ground and fit from a recent run, his main query is that indifferent form a few starts back.

runners_data.name: Calyxoh
runners_data.note: Recent Flat winner (form showing a 7 in the string) who holds a tongue-tie, but his true running style is that of a hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield slot by the crowded rear of this field; the 7-day turnaround for Patrick Morris and a modest Good-turf strike rate (1W from 8 runners) temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Calyxoh's formline is modest, with several rear-of-field efforts and no win in his last five starts, yet he rates far higher on our figures than that suggests. Quick to run again seven days on and proven over today's trip and ground, finding that level remains the obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Thankfully
runners_data.note: Burke's 3-year-old is winless on Good turf (0-from-2 strikes on similar going) but placed at 8f on Soft suggests staying power; Pat Cosgrave adds class in the saddle and a prominent racing style gives her a live chance if the pace is genuinely honest.
runners_data.comment: Thankfully was unplaced last time out. That followed a win three starts back, with a third deeper in her form. She rates only midfield on our figures, has form over today's trip and ground, and carries 128lb from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Crazee Icon
runners_data.note: Balding's 3-year-old has placed five times including twice at 7f on Good, and a prominent-to-midfield style suits Chester; Jason Watson takes the ride and the 29-day freshener looks fine — consistent form makes this horse a credible player if getting a clean passage around the bends.
runners_data.comment: Crazee Icon won last time out and has rarely been out of the frame this spell, with two seconds among her other starts, yet she anchors our figures at the bottom of this field. Proven over today's trip and ground, she carries 123lb from stall 4 and needs more to figure.

races.paceDynamic: Start Me Up is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to push the fractions hard from the outset, should settle into a controlled, sustainable gallop around Chester's tight circuit over this 7½f trip. The prominent types — Knights Gold, Thankfully, and Crazee Icon — will sit just behind but none are natural pace-pressers, meaning the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching on Good ground. Mission Command and Calyxoh are both genuine hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear, so their true closing positions will be harder to achieve than the race map implies, blunting the effectiveness of a late-run scenario. This race shape — a single uncontested pace-setter on a fair gallop, with hold-up horses displaced and struggling to get daylight around Chester's turns — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and pounce from close to the pace in the straight, making the prominent-to-midfield profile the standout beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Start Me Up Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Start Me Up leads unchallenged and the gallop remains honest enough to soften rivals but not slow enough to spark a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Start Me Up gets his own way in front on Good ground, controlling fractions and kicking off the home turn to put the race to bed; his recent wins at 7f and 6f on similar surfaces show he handles this trip range under these conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to stretch the field and a close-tracking prominent horse pounces after the home turn.
scenarios.body: Knights Gold or Thankfully close throughout and benefit from a well-run race that negates the front runner's advantage in the final furlong; Chester's tight finish rewards horses saving ground and travelling sweetly into the bend.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses slightly and a horse sitting mid-division finds a clear run in the straight to pick off fading rivals.
scenarios.body: Crazee Icon or Sujet, travelling well off a steady gallop, find room on the inside and pick off the leader inside the final furlong; this requires a near-perfect run through traffic on Chester's narrow straight, which is an inherent risk.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Closers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely fast, the field strings out, and genuine hold-up horses overcome their redistributed positions to close from well off the pace.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely outcome given Mission Command and Calyxoh are displaced from their natural positions, making a long sweeping finish-line raid extremely difficult on this track configuration; only a truly burning gallop would open this scenario, and Start Me Up alone rarely sets one.

watchPoints.text: Start Me Up (Jack Callan) — watch whether he is allowed to stride straight to the front unchallenged at the start; if he gets a soft lead through the first two furlongs, this race shape is effectively set.

Mission Command and Calyxoh — both genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield slots; watch how much daylight they find on the far side of Chester's tight turns, as a bottleneck could end their race prematurely.

Knights Gold — watch his position through the opening two furlongs; if he can slot prominently behind the leader rather than being shuffled back, his consistent placed form at 8f on Good makes him dangerous in the home straight.

Thankfully (Pat Cosgrave) — K. R. Burke's 9-from-51 T14 strike rate is strong and Cosgrave's tactical intelligence on a track that rewards good positioning is worth monitoring if she is ridden with intent from the gate.

Crazee Icon — watch how Jason Watson navigates the tight Chester bends from mid-division; if he can hug the rail and avoid trouble, his placed form at 7f on Good could be activated in the final furlong.

races.name: Raymond & Kathleen Corbett Memorial City Plate Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Holguin
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form (three wins and a place at 7f on Good), Faleh Bugheniam has ridden this track and trip before, and the horse's prominent style maps perfectly to Chester's short run-in — 63 days off is the only mild query but the trainer has a modest recent record.|
runners_data.comment: Holguin won two starts back, after back-to-back thirds, then could finish only sixth last time out. He returns from a 63-day break, proven over today's trip and going, and races from stall 8, third on our figures at 108.

runners_data.name: Myal
runners_data.note: David Allan gives this horse a terrific record at the trip on Good ground (two wins and a place from nine similar runs), and the prominent style is ideally suited to sitting just off Witness Stand's controlled lead on a track where prominent racers dominate.|
runners_data.comment: Myal was runner-up again last time out, a win two starts back proving he retains his mark, with only a below-par fifth three starts back interrupting the run. Fourth on our figures at 106 and effective over today's trip and going from stall 7, he returns after a 63-day gap.

runners_data.name: Palmar Bay
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly has placed at Grade level and the jockey Sean Bowen offers tactical awareness, but hold-up horses must be discounted on Chester's tight, turning track — her last five runs show consistent midfield-to-rear finishes and she needs traffic to collapse.|
runners_data.comment: Palmar Bay has been the model of consistency with three straight fourths but followed that with an unplaced effort last time out. Proven over today's trip and going, he's sixth on our figures at 102 from stall 4, having last run 42 days ago.

runners_data.name: Roman Dragon
runners_data.note: Carries a cheekpiece (v) and has been off 21 days, but the flagged tendency to fade in the finish is a serious concern on a track that punishes those who cannot sustain effort through the bend; 24/14 hit-rate on Good is superficially good but the recent form string (701800) betrays a horse not at its best.|
runners_data.comment: Roman Dragon's only win in six recent starts came four starts back, but he has been well held in each of his last two starts. Bottom of our figures at 95, though he does have today's trip and going in his favour, running from stall 9, 21 days since his last run.

runners_data.name: Tiber Flow
runners_data.note: 427 days between runs is a huge question mark for William Haggas, but the three wins from 11 runs at 7f on Good ground, including a second at this trip last time, mark this horse as a serious player if the layoff hasn't blunted the edge — prominent style suits Chester ideally.|
runners_data.comment: Tiber Flow was a good second last time out, backing up a win three starts back, and that form leaves him second on our figures at 110. A near 14-month absence is the obvious query, but today's trip and going are both proven, and he races from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Witness Stand
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner carrying a tongue-tie (tp) and a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 suggests this horse is racing out of its most comfortable role; the recent form (00-082) is modest, and while it will control tempo, there is a real question whether it can then sustain the effort through the home straight against fresher rivals.|
runners_data.comment: Witness Stand tops our figures at 116 following a clear second last time out, a return to form after a run of below-par efforts. Yet to score in this sequence, he has today's trip and going in his favour and returns from a 35-day break out of stall 6.

runners_data.name: Dash Of Azure
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent type that Ralph Beckett has in form (8/48 T14), but with several horses wanting that position the horse is likely to find itself squeezed away from its natural berth — STYLE_FIT of 0.92 tempers confidence, and the 14-day turnaround may help freshness without solving the positional problem.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in recent starts, Dash Of Azure ran her best race last time out when runner-up after two below-par efforts. Seventh on our figures at 101 with today's trip and going both proven, she's back within a fortnight from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Five Ways
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's three-year-old won on Straight and Standard ground but the step up in trip to 7f at Chester, combined with being nudged out of its favoured prominent slot by stronger rivals, makes this a difficult race; the weight allowance is an asset but STYLE_FIT concerns limit the upside.|
runners_data.comment: Five Ways won five starts back but the form has tailed off since, unplaced last time out after a run of one-paced efforts. Fifth on our figures at 105, he has today's trip and going in his favour from stall 5, 28 days on from that latest run.

runners_data.name: Northern Champion
runners_data.note: Two wins at 6-7f on Good this season show genuine ability, but the three-year-old is meeting older horses rated 7-11lb higher and will be competing with several others for limited prominent positions — if the redistribution leaves him buried mid-pack, his chance effectively dissolves on this track.|
runners_data.comment: Northern Champion twice won in the middle of this sequence but has since flopped into ninth last time out, following an unplaced effort before that. Eighth on our figures at 99, he has today's trip and going in his favour from stall 1, 22 days since his last run.

races.paceDynamic: Witness Stand is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine speed horse to push them along, should be able to control tempo from the outset on Chester's tight, turning 7f track — a course that heavily rewards those who can dictate and avoid traffic complications. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching on Good ground, meaning the race will be run at a measured, sustainable gallop that suits those sitting just off the leader rather than those forced to make up ground late. Holguin, Myal, and Tiber Flow are the natural prominent types best placed to track Witness Stand in the second tier and pounce in the short home straight. This shape is a clear fit for prominent racers who can travel comfortably on the heels of a lone leader and produce a quick, decisive effort in the final furlong — hold-up horses such as Palmar Bay and Roman Dragon face a stiff ask on a track that rarely rewards late-running. The field contains more prominent-type runners than the map can accommodate: Northern Champion, Dash Of Azure, and Five Ways are genuine early-position horses who will be competing for limited ground near the pace — Witness Stand and Myal are most likely to actually secure their favoured slots given draw and freshness.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Witness Stand Controls, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Witness Stand dictates an uncontested, sustainable pace on Good ground and the prominent trackers pounce through the short home stretch.
scenarios.body: Witness Stand's controlled lead allows Holguin and Myal to travel well in second and third before unleashing finishing kicks in the final furlong, where Chester's tight circuit gives little time for hold-up horses to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Fractured Pace, Prominent Runners Battle
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Northern Champion, Dash Of Azure, and Five Ways causes scrimmaging near the pace and lifts the tempo early.
scenarios.body: The contested early gallop string the field out wider and faster, suiting a horse like Tiber Flow who has the class to sit in behind a stronger pace and produce a sustained finish having not had to burn energy in positional fighting.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sneaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses early and the home-straight scramble creates a gap for a closer to thread through.
scenarios.body: Palmar Bay, needing a truly congested tempo to make up the ground from the rear on a tight track, would benefit most from a bunched-up final furlong where her one-pace closing style can catch tiring leaders; Roman Dragon's headgear and proven form in similar going is an outside factor but the fade warning tempers expectations.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Long-Shot Benefit, Youth Beats Age
scenarios.trigger: If the younger three-year-olds Five Ways or Northern Champion bounce off a fast opening quarter and steal a march on their heavier-weighted rivals.
scenarios.body: Three-year-olds receive a weight allowance and either could exploit a tactical advantage if they secure an uncontested early slot, though both carry style-fit concerns having been pushed back from their natural position in the field — the probability remains low given competing prominent types around them.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Dash Of Azure, Five Ways, and Northern Champion create a contested early pace — if all three push to claim prominent positions, they could lift the tempo beyond what suits Witness Stand's controlled front-running plan.|

Tiber Flow's 427-day absence is the single biggest uncertainty in the race; monitor the market for support or drift, as Haggas horses returning from long breaks can be very well prepared or still needing the run.|

Roman Dragon's fade warning is significant at Chester where horses must sustain effort around a tight bend with little room to recover — any signs of greenness or hanging in the closing stages could cause interference.|

Witness Stand sets the race tempo from stall one, so watch how quickly Jack Doughty allows the horse to settle into its lead — a slow, controlled opening will compress the race into a sprint finish that may ultimately flatter the prominent trackers rather than the leader itself.|

Holguin's trainer Hamad Al Jehani has a modest T14 record (0/12) which is worth noting in the context of a 63-day absence — if the horse comes to hand quickly under Bugheniam it is the one to beat, but an out-of-sorts display cannot be ruled out given the handler's recent form.|

races.name: Excell Supply Handicap

runners_data.name: Art Lover
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner returning after a 276-day absence, which is a significant unknown; bred for hold-up racing and drops into a flat 6f handicap at Chester where getting a clear run on the tight circuit is the key tactical challenge, but in-running form shows a win and a place at this trip in similar going.
runners_data.comment: Art Lover scored three starts back. A close second four starts back sits alongside it, form that stacks up on our figures despite two below-par efforts since. He has today's trip and ground covered and carries 135lb from stall 2, though a 276-day absence is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Grasmere Boy
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed pace-setter, his three-run form of 221 is compact and progressive, and Dylan Hogan should be able to dictate from the front on Good ground that suits; the big question is whether a horse comfortable going prominent can sustain the effort over Chester's unusual 6f layout without being reeled in late.
runners_data.comment: Grasmere Boy won last time out having been runner-up in his previous two starts, a strong recent sequence. He has raced over today's trip and ground before and carries 135lb from stall 1, though he rates only midfield on our figures for this in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Inca Heights
runners_data.note: Clive Cox runner who has been consistently disappointing in recent starts (9th, 13th, 12th, flagged as fading in the finish) and the 3lb claim from Jack Callan provides minimal compensation for a horse that has not threatened competitively in Good ground over this trip for some time.
runners_data.comment: Inca Heights has been unplaced in three of his last five starts and remains without a win in that spell, yet he rates highly on our figures. Proven over today's trip and ground, he carries 132lb from stall 4, with 47 days off the main query.

runners_data.name: Kind Touch
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey yard in fair form (6/56 over 14 days) and this horse has a genuine win and place at 6f in Good-to-Soft/Good conditions; prominent style makes it one of the more naturally suited runners to track the pace without burning excessive energy, and the form string of 12-37 contains encouraging early efforts.
runners_data.comment: Kind Touch landed one of his last four starts and tops our figures by a clear margin here. He has form over today's trip and ground and carries 132lb from stall 3, with only a below-par run last time out as a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Polka Blue
runners_data.note: Charles Hills runner who arrives on the back of a decent recent run 15 days ago with a form sequence containing two wins; naturally a prominent racer whose preferred position is compromised in this field, meaning Jason Watson may have to ride more conservatively than ideal — that slight style compromise tempers its chance despite solid underlying form.
runners_data.comment: Polka Blue won two starts in a row before finishing third last time out, a formline that reads consistently well. She has form over today's trip and ground, carries 128lb from stall 6, but sits only midfield on our figures for this.

runners_data.name: Cotai Lights
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's runner is back just five days after its last start — a freshness flag — and its recent form (339400) contains a string of below-par efforts in Good ground; naturally prominent but squeezed out of that position by race shape, and Donagh Murphy faces a difficult tactical task with a horse that has shown little in similar conditions.
runners_data.comment: Cotai Lights has been unplaced in his last two starts and remains without a win in his last six, but he owns one of the sharpest speed figures here and returns quickly just five days on. Proven over today's trip and ground, he carries 128lb from stall 8, with rediscovering his placed form the target.

runners_data.name: Kody B
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's three-year-old carries hold-up style credentials and won over 6f in Soft going 55 days ago; David Allan is an experienced northern jockey who will be patient, but Chester's tight circuit can frustrate genuine hold-up horses who rely on a straight to deliver their challenge.
runners_data.comment: Kody B landed a race three starts back but has been below par since, and he rates near the bottom of this field on our figures. He does have form over today's trip and ground, but a 55-day absence adds to the task from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Sargent Dennis
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's charge arrives on the back of a strong form sequence (5221) including a win in Good ground at this trip 61 days ago; genuine prominent tendencies mean Edward Greatrex may push forward more aggressively than the race map shows, and if the style restriction eases slightly this horse has the raw form to be competitive.
runners_data.comment: Sargent Dennis won last time out and was runner-up in each of his previous two starts, form that reads well on paper. He has form over today's distance but anchors our figures at the bottom of this field, with his trainer out of form at just 5% in the last 14 days.

races.paceDynamic: Grasmere Boy is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him from the gates on Chester's tight 6f circuit, he should be able to control fractions and set a sustainable, metronomic pace rather than a lung-busting gallop. Kind Touch and Inca Heights have prominent tendencies but are unlikely to challenge Grasmere Boy for the rail position, meaning the pace is essentially dictated by one horse without pressure — a scenario that historically rewards those who can sit a length or two off the leader and pounce on the bend into the straight. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position: Polka Blue, Cotai Lights, and Sargent Dennis are genuine prominent racers but have been redistributed to midfield because the space simply does not exist for them to race where they prefer, with Polka Blue and Sargent Dennis most likely to push closer than their mapped position suggests given their recent form. With one uncontested pace-setter shaping a controlled tempo, the tactical verdict is clear: horses who can track the leader in second or third — particularly those not burning energy fighting for position — are most advantaged, with a hold-up horse needing an exceptionally strong finishing kick to bridge the gap in time on this sharp, turning track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Grasmere Boy Controls, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Grasmere Boy leads unchallenged and sets a steady, uncontested gallop that leaves just enough in the tank for the closers.
scenarios.body: Grasmere Boy dictates from the front but the controlled pace means horses tracking him in second and third have energy to deliver a telling challenge in the final furlong; Chester's sharp turn into the straight rewards those who travel smoothly in the leader's wake rather than those who chase from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Grasmere Boy is permitted to set an even easier pace than expected and capitalises on a soft lead to score wire-to-wire.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to push Grasmere Boy at any stage, he controls the gallop to the point where his rivals are always chasing a target they can never quite reach; his recent winning form over this trip in Good ground and the absence of pace pressure makes this a genuine, if secondary, possibility.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Emerge From Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the pace scenario plays out slowly enough to compress the field, allowing Art Lover or Kody B to deliver a late run.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow tempo would see the entire field bunch approaching the home turn, negating Grasmere Boy's lead advantage and bringing hold-up types into play in the final 100 yards; however, Chester's tight geometry generally punishes those who have to find gaps, limiting how likely this is to fully materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Reigns
scenarios.trigger: If redistributed prominent types Polka Blue, Cotai Lights, or Sargent Dennis surge forward early and create a contested, faster-than-expected pace that burns out the front group.
scenarios.body: A more competitive early fractions scenario would see Grasmere Boy pressed hard and potentially stopping in the final furlong, opening the door to a horse who has conserved energy from the rear; this shape depends heavily on horses racing outside their natural mapped position, making it the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Grasmere Boy's early pace control is the race's pivot — if Dylan Hogan is allowed to dictate unchallenged through the first two furlongs, the entire race shape is set; watch whether any of Polka Blue, Kind Touch or Sargent Dennis pushes for the early lead and disrupts that dynamic.

Polka Blue and Sargent Dennis are natural prominent types forced to race further back than they prefer — if either jockey decides to push forward regardless, it could force a faster early tempo than expected and compromise their own chance as well as Grasmere Boy's.

Art Lover returns from a 276-day layoff for William Haggas — horses returning from such a long absence can be either ring-rusty or fresh and cherry-ripe; monitor market moves closer to post time as stable confidence will be the key signal.

Cotai Lights ran just five days ago, which on a tight turning track like Chester could manifest as jaded early pace or a reluctance to engage in the closing stages — Donagh Murphy's tactics in the first furlong will reveal whether this horse is truly fit to fire.

Chester's 6f circuit places a premium on a clean, wide-open passage around the home bend — horses drawn in lower stalls (inner) have an inherent advantage tracking the pace, and any runner caught wide turning for home will likely lose vital lengths regardless of how the pace scenario unfolds.

races.name: Minuty, The Spirit Of Saint-Tropez Handicap

runners_data.name: Fast Fred
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has finished 1st and 2nd in two of his last three on good ground over 12f, and the step up to 14.5f here looks well within range; 14 days since last run keeps him at peak readiness and David Allan's bold front-tracking style suits Chester's enclosed layout perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Fast Fred won five starts back and confirmed that level with a runner-up effort soon after, though his last two starts have been below that standard. Third on our figures at 80 with today's trip and going both proven, he was last seen out just 14 days ago.

runners_data.name: Nibras Gold
runners_data.note: Trainer James Owen sends him out with a solid 14-day strike rate and the horse has strong sim-going credentials (13/15), but the 301-day absence is a sizeable concern for an eight-year-old asked to lead at a track that demands instant sharpness; he is the confirmed pace-setter and his role is crucial to how this race unfolds regardless of his own winning chance.
runners_data.comment: Nibras Gold won three starts back and also opened this sequence with a win, sandwiching a below-form sixth in between, before rounding off with a solid second last time out. Sixth on our figures at 76, with today's trip and going both in his favour.

runners_data.name: L'eagle Aid
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston has runners in sharp form (9/67 14-day) and Sean Bowen adds valuable tactical nous; L'eagle Aid has a frustrating string of sixth-place finishes but consistently runs at 12f on good ground and the extra yardage today may be enough to unlock a place effort from a prominent position.
runners_data.comment: L'Eagle Aid strung together three sixths and a fifth, before stepping forward last time out with a clear third, suggesting his form is on the up. Yet to score in this sequence, he sits second on our figures at 81 with today's trip and going both proven, seen out only 14 days ago.

runners_data.name: Dream Harder
runners_data.note: Six consecutive sixth-place finishes tells its own story and Mark Loughnane has drawn a blank in his last 20 runs; a hold-up profile on a track that rewards those close to the pace is an additional structural disadvantage, and nothing in the recent form recommends confidence here.
runners_data.comment: Dream Harder has finished sixth in all five of his recent starts, yet still tops our figures at 82 on residual promise. His stable is winless from its last 20 runners, an added concern, and today's trip and going are already proven, 24 days since his latest run.

runners_data.name: Just An Hour
runners_data.note: Naturally a prominent racer with a fine record of placed efforts (3W7P sim-going) who has been pushed into midfield on the map because the prominent berths are over-subscribed; Jason Watson is a capable claimer of ground but the horse will need to find racing room on a circuit where that is not always straightforward when out of his preferred front-half position.
runners_data.comment: Just An Hour was runner-up three starts back and backed that up with a solid third last time out, sandwiching a below-form sixth in between. Yet to score in this sequence, he's fourth on our figures at 80 with today's trip and going both proven, seen out 27 days ago.

runners_data.name: Spartan Times
runners_data.note: Genuine pace horse with a recent win at 16f on good ground and a strong overall record (3W4P) — but with Nibras Gold taking the lead and Fast Fred and L'eagle Aid filling the prominent slots, he is likely to be operating further back than he wants; Joey Haynes will need to manage that carefully if the horse is to have any chance of recapturing his best.
runners_data.comment: Spartan Times won four starts back and has stayed competitive since, with a third along the way, before a runner-up effort last time out. Second-bottom on our figures at 72, with today's trip and going both proven, he was last seen out a fortnight ago.

runners_data.name: Robusto
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton sends him out freshened after 18 days and Edward Greatrex is a steady pilot, but a sim-going score of just 2/15 on good turf is a glaring red flag, and his hold-up profile puts him structurally last in the queue in a race unlikely to see a truly searching pace that he can close into.
runners_data.comment: Robusto won three starts back but the form has since gone off the boil, only fifth and eighth in his last two. Fifth on our figures at 78, with today's trip and going both proven, 18 days since his latest run.

runners_data.name: Spirit Catcher
runners_data.note: Showed gritty form with back-to-back seconds and a win in his last three good-ground runs, so the ability is present — naturally a hold-up horse who has been shown in midfield due to the redistribution of rear-end types, meaning Donagh Murphy (7lb claimer) will need things to fall right in a race where the pace may be too steady for a finishing effort to materialise.
runners_data.comment: Spirit Catcher won five starts back and ran a pair of placed efforts after that, but the formline has since tailed off with a fifth last time out. Bottom of our figures at 71, though today's trip and going are both proven, seen out a fortnight ago.

races.paceDynamic: Nibras Gold is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no rival likely to genuinely dispute the lead from the gates, he should control matters from the front at a sustainable gallop around Chester's tight, turning circuit. Fast Fred and L'eagle Aid are the natural prominent horses best placed to track him, with the field otherwise containing a cluster of pace types — Just An Hour, Spartan Times, and to a lesser extent Spirit Catcher — who cannot all occupy their preferred forward positions and will be squeezed into midfield roles they are not drawn to. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can secure their natural berths; Nibras Gold is overwhelmingly most likely to lead, with Fast Fred and L'eagle Aid the next best placed to get close to the early pace. A controlled, single-paced gallop set by Nibras Gold on a flat, fair surface suits horses who can sit close to a modest tempo and sustain their effort into the straight — making race-fit, prominent-to-midfield stalkers the primary beneficiaries, with deep closers unlikely to generate the ground they need if the pace is never truly pressured.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nibras Gold Controls, Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Nibras Gold leads comfortably and the pace remains honest-but-sustainable, allowing close-tracking types to strike turning in.
scenarios.body: Nibras Gold dictates from the front at a rhythm that suits those directly behind him, meaning Fast Fred and L'eagle Aid — both fit, on-form, and proven at comparable distances on good ground — can travel smoothly before challenging in the final two furlongs. Chester's unique circuit rewards those who race prominently without being buried in traffic, and these two have the course-suitable profiles to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Nibras Gold Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If Nibras Gold's long absence (301 days) proves no barrier and the field is slow to pick up when he kicks, leaving him to grind clear.
scenarios.body: After a prolonged layoff, Nibras Gold has nonetheless shown high sim-going scores (13/15) and his trainer's 14-day strike rate is healthy; if the field underestimates his fitness and allows him to dictate unchallenged with a decisive move, he could steal a march. The tight, enclosed nature of Chester means those tracking from midfield may encounter interference as they try to close, gifting the lead horse extra advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Emerge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough to string the field out and those pushed into midfield generate a sweeping late run.
scenarios.body: Just An Hour and Spartan Times are genuine prominent types operating out of role in midfield; if they settle better than expected and the gallop is true, they can deliver a sustained late challenge rather than the usual finishing burst. However, both carry STYLE_FIT discounts and their out-of-role mapping means this shape depends on horses doing something they are not naturally drawn to do.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpectedly strong pace causes early casualties and Robusto or Spirit Catcher come from well off it to collect.
scenarios.body: Robusto and Spirit Catcher are genuine hold-up horses whose rare good-ground form (2/15 and 9/15 sim-going scores respectively) makes this scenario a low-probability event relying on conditions that don't currently exist. Spirit Catcher, though mapped to midfield due to redistribution, retains natural hold-up tendencies that only pay off if the race truly falls apart at the front.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Just An Hour or Spartan Times — both natural prominent types squeezed into midfield — attempt to push forward early and create a scrappy, competitive pace that destabilises Nibras Gold's intended solo lead.

Nibras Gold's 301-day absence is the single biggest variable in the race; if he shows any signs of ring-rustiness in the first half-mile and surrenders the lead, the entire pace shape collapses and the midfield pack will find it chaotic.

Chester's tight turns create serious traffic risks for horses running from midfield or hold-up positions — Spirit Catcher and Robusto are both likely to face congestion in the back straight and will need a clear passage that may not materialise.

Fast Fred's recent course-and-distance profile (1st and 2nd at 12f on good) combined with 14 days freshness makes him the horse to time your sectional tracking against — his response to Nibras Gold at the two-furlong pole will define how many can win.

races.name: Bootleg Beatles Live At Chester Apprentice Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Venezuelan
runners_data.note: The confirmed front runner who shapes as the likely pace-setter for the entire field; 14 days since last run, visor worn, and his four previous Good-ground runs produced only one win suggesting he can be vulnerable if tracked closely, but with no obvious challenger he should dictate comfortably — racing prominently is his natural mode but the STYLE_FIT tag reflects some reduction in confidence given the competitive context.
runners_data.comment: Venezuelan won this sequence's oldest start and was runner-up in the two starts that followed, before a below-form eighth and a fourth in his last two. Tops our figures at 86, with today's going already proven, seen out a fortnight ago.

runners_data.name: Imperial Sovereign
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer at his best over staying trips, with four of his last five runs at 14f-16f and a third on Good ground last time out — his 0W1P similar-going record tempers enthusiasm but he remains capable of a late rattle if the pace is honest enough to bring him into it.
runners_data.comment: Imperial Sovereign's best effort in this sequence was a third four starts back, and he's continued to run creditably since with a seventh, a sixth and a fourth. Yet to score, he's third on our figures at 84 with today's trip and going both proven, seen out a fortnight ago.

runners_data.name: Heathen
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who was third at this course and distance (16f Good) most recently, giving him a directly relevant course and trip angle; the 42-day break is worth monitoring, but Jennie Candlish's yard is 2/23 in the past fortnight suggesting the team is operating at modest strike rate.
runners_data.comment: Heathen has been the model of consistency with three fourths and a second, following up with a third last time out. Yet to score, he sits second on our figures at 85 with a leading speed figure of 86, both trip and going proven, 42 days since his last run.

runners_data.name: Tailorman
runners_data.note: Returning from 301 days off which is the most significant flag in this field — however, Ian Williams's runner last won at 16f on Good and has course form at this trip, and the prominent style fits this race shape naturally; his headgear note (hg:p) and solid similar-going record (10/15, 2W6P) make him a fascinating returning type if fit.
runners_data.comment: Tailorman won four starts back but hasn't been seen since finishing fourth 301 days ago, a huge layoff that dominates his profile. His stable is also without a winner from its last 28 runners, and although today's trip and going are both proven, he's hard to back.

runners_data.name: Curran
runners_data.note: Won over 14f on Good ground and clearly has the ability, but his natural hold-up style means he has been pushed into a midfield mapping here — in a race where Venezuelan controls the pace at a modest clip, Curran is unlikely to be presented with the strong gallop he needs to close from off the pace, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.
runners_data.comment: Curran was sixth last time out. He scored two starts back, and was unplaced three starts back. Fifth on our figures at 76 with today's trip and going both proven, seen out a fortnight ago.

runners_data.name: Vaguely Royal
runners_data.note: Has run well in similar-going conditions in thirds (twice at 16f) but the visor and repeated placed efforts without a win at this level raise a consistency question; mapped to midfield rather than his preferred hold-up berth because the field is crowded with late runners, and a slow to moderate pace will leave him with little room to deliver.
runners_data.comment: Vaguely Royal strung together three straight thirds, but tailed off to a sixth last time out. Yet to score, he's sixth on our figures at 75; his stable has managed just one success from 47 runners lately, though today's trip and going are both proven, 40 days since his last run.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Approach
runners_data.note: A young 3-year-old trained by Charlie Johnston who sent out nine winners from 59 runners in the past fortnight — excellent trainer form — and the horse has won twice over 14f on Good, with today's step up to 1m6½f the key unknown; if the trip is within range, his ability to travel close to the pace makes him dangerous.
runners_data.comment: Gaelic Approach has won twice in his last six starts, each success flanked by a runner-up effort, though he was below form when unplaced last time out. Fourth on our figures at 78, with today's trip and going both proven, seen out 17 days ago.

runners_data.name: Mudita
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose preferred front-end position is crowded out by Venezuelan and the other pace types — Fahey's yard is in good form but the 3-year-old faces a big step up in trip from his best form at 10f-12f, and being forced to race in midfield rather than forward is an additional complication.
runners_data.comment: Mudita won three starts back and has run respectably since, a third last time out her latest effort. Bottom of our figures at 67, though today's going is proven, seen out three weeks ago.

races.paceDynamic: Venezuelan is the one confirmed front runner here and, with no meaningful challenger for the lead over 1m6½f at Chester's tight, turning circuit, he should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. Heathen and Tailorman are the other prominent types most likely to secure early positions just behind Venezuelan, with Tailorman's recent headgear and course-suitable profile making him the likelier of the two to slot in on his shoulder. This field contains more prominent and hold-up horses than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Mudita, Curran, and Vaguely Royal are genuine front-runners or prominent types who are likely to end up racing out of their preferred position, compressed into midfield, which undermines their chances in any shape that depends on them executing from that position. The combination of one uncontested leader setting a measured pace over this stamina trip at a turning track strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort into the straight, rather than those relying on a late run from off a genuinely strong pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Venezuelan Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Venezuelan leads unopposed at a fair pace and the race develops into a test of sustained stamina from the front.
scenarios.body: Venezuelan sets a manageable tempo on the Chester circuit and those positioned just behind — Tailorman and Heathen — have the jumping-off point to challenge as the field straightens; Gaelic Approach, stepping up markedly in trip but trained by Charlie Johnston who excels with improvers, is also well-placed to run on from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Venezuelan's gallop proves just strong enough that Heathen or Tailorman can track and overhaul him in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A marginally stronger pace than expected stretches the field and the two prominent trackers are close enough to pick Venezuelan off without needing a finishing kick; Tailorman's winning form at this course and trip combination makes him the more dangerous of the pair in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If Venezuelan sets a strong enough gallop that the hold-up horses — those with genuine stamina — can close powerfully in the straight.
scenarios.body: Imperial Sovereign and Gaelic Approach, both capable of finishing off longer distances when a true pace is set, would be the beneficiaries; however, this scenario is compromised by the fact that Curran and Vaguely Royal — the other apparent closers — are redistributed prominent types unlikely to be in their natural position to produce a telling late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Venezuelan is taken on early or backs off dramatically, creating a messy, crawling race that develops into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A compressed, tactical race would scramble all pace profiles and make the result highly unpredictable, but Gaelic Approach's turn of foot and Tailorman's proven ability on good ground give them a marginal edge in a late dash; this is the least likely shape given Venezuelan's likely willingness to bowl along unchallenged.

watchPoints.text: Tailorman's 301-day absence is the single biggest risk factor in the race — if he returns to full fitness he has the profile, going record, and prominent style to win, but that layoff could mean he needs the run.

Mudita and Curran are both likely to be racing out of their natural style — watch whether Ethan Tindall on Mudita attempts to push forward regardless, which could unsettle Venezuelan's intended solo lead and alter the pace shape entirely.

Gaelic Approach represents Charlie Johnston's powerful in-form yard and the 3-year-old has a course and distance question at 1m6½f — if he gets a prominent pitch behind Venezuelan the stamina question becomes the sole decider.

Venezuelan's rider Zoe Lewis claims 7lbs — at the weights that represents a meaningful allowance for the likely pace-setter, and if the weight edge allows him to sustain his lead longer than expected the race could be over sooner than rivals anticipate.

Both Vaguely Royal and Imperial Sovereign have finishing position histories that suggest they need a genuinely run race — monitor early fractions because a falsely slow gallop will leave both short of a target to aim at in the closing stages.
